senses.gloss:
अब्धि Tatpur. m. (-धिः)
 ^1 The ocean; lit. and figur.; e. g.
(figur.) in the Nalodaya: अपि यो दायादाय क्षयप्रदोऽहंसि
सतां यदाया दायः । करमादायादाय श्रियोऽब्धिरधिराज-
मसिगदायादा यः; or in the Rudrayāmalat.: सदा सेव्यो देवैः
स भवति नरो भक्तिसुलभः । स जीवन्मुक्तोऽपि तरति च भवा-
ब्धिमचिरतः.
 ^2 The name of one of the attendants of the
Sun (acc. to Vyāḍi on Hemach.).
 ^3 (In mathematical lan-
guage sometimes used to denote) the numeral 4; e. g. in
Brahmagupta's Brāhmasiddhānta: परिवर्ताखचतुष्टयशराब्धि-
रसगुणयमद्विवसुतिथयः (comp. Colebr. As. Res. XII. p. 231
note); or कस्यासौ घटिकासंघो द्युगणस्य यदुद्भवम् । पञ्चाभ्र-
चन्द्राब्धिमितं विधोर्मण्डलशेषकम्; or in the Keralagrantha, as
quoted by Rādhāk. (s. v. अभिघात): अभिघातं स्यात्पूर्वं वेद-
द्वित्र्यब्धिवर्णाश्चेत् । नगवर्गाणां परतो धरणीचन्द्रद्विरामाढ्याः;
or in the Sūryasiddh. quoted Journ. As. XVI. p. 35. 1. 12.
Schlegel is probably correct when he ascribes this use of
the word to the division of the ocean according to the four
cardinal points of the compass (Refl. sur l'étude des langues
as. p. 198), but he is mistaken when he adds, that ‘ocean’
may designate also the numeral 7, for all the synonymes
of this word are only used to denote 4; comp. E. Jacquet
Journ. As. vol. XVI. (1835) p. 17. 104. and, besides Raffles
[]
quoted there, Humboldt's Kawi Sprache I. p. 32.--E. अप्
and धि.

अब्धिकण Tatpur. m. (-णः) Probably an incorrect reading
instead of अब्धिकफ q. v. E. अब्धि and कण.

अब्धिकफ Tatpur. m. (-फः)
 ^1 Froth, foam.
 ^2 Cuttle fish bone,
the dorsal scale of the cuttle fish (Sepia officinalis); so
called because it looks like the froth of the sea; Rāyamu-
kuṭa &c.: अब्धेः कफ इव. Compare समुद्रकफ, अब्धिफेन,
अर्णवमल and the following. E. अब्धि and कफ.

अब्धिज Tatpur. 1. m. f. n. (-जः-जा-जम्) Born in or by the
ocean.
2.
 a. m. sing. (-जः)
 ^1 The moon; comp. अब्ज.
 ^2 (In
mathematical language sometimes used to denote) the nu-
meral 1.
 ^3 Cuttle fish bone; the same as अब्धिकफ or स-
मुद्रफेन (according to the Nigh. Prak.), comp. also अर्णवज.
(The meaning ‘moon’ is not given in the Koshas; but as
the word occurs in the second meaning, in a mathematical
Index, similarly as अमृतदीधिति, and as the synonymes
of चन्द्र q. v. are used likewise so, it seemed to me neces-
sary to infer this mathematical application from the mean-
ing ‘moon’, which would arise from the etymon of the
word in the same way as अब्ज 2. 1. q. v. Comp. also श्वे-
तधामन् ‘moon and cuttle fish bone’.)
 b. m. du. (-जौ) A name of the Aśvins q. v., these two
gods having sprung from the ocean when it was churned
for the amṛta.
3. n. (-जम्) Salt (according to the Nigh. Prak.).
4. f. (-जा) Spirituous liquor; see सुरा, the latter hav-
ing come from the ocean when it was churned for the amṛta.
E. अब्धि and ज.
अब्धिझष Tatpur. m. (-षः) A sea fish. E. अब्धि and झष.

अब्धिडिण्डर Tatpur. m. (-रः) Cuttle fish bone; the same as
समुद्रफेन or अब्धिकफ q. v., (according to the Nigh. Prak.);
comp. अब्धिहिण्डीर, and डिण्डिर, डिण्डीर, दिण्डीर,
हिण्डिर, हिण्डीर. E. अब्धि and डिण्डर.

अब्धिद्वीपा Bahuvr. f. (-पा) The earth. E. अब्धि and द्वीपा;
lit. ‘having islands formed by the ocean’.

अब्धिनगरी Tatpur. f. (-री) The ocean-city, a name of Dvā-
rakā, the capital of Kṛṣṇa. E. अब्धि and नगरी.

अब्धिनवनीतक Tatpur. m. (-कः) The moon; comp. अब्ज 2. 1.
E. अब्धि and नवनीतक.

अब्धिफल Tatpur. n. (-लम्) The name of a fruit, used as a
drug; also called समुद्रफल. E. अब्धि and फल.

अब्धिफेन Tatpur. m. (-नः) The same as अब्धिकफ q. v.; comp.
समुद्रफेन. E. अब्धि and फेन.

अब्धिमण्डूकी Tatpur. f. (-की) The pearl oyster. E. अब्धि
and मण्डूकी.

अब्धिशयन Bahuvr. m. (-नः) A name of Viṣṇu; (lit. having
the ocean for his couch, i. e. sleeping on the ocean at the
periods of the destruction and renovation of the world).
E. अब्धि and शयन.

अब्धिसार Tatpur. m. (-रः) A jewel, a gem (Nigh. Prak.
= रत्न). E. अब्धि and सार.

अब्धिहिण्डीर Tatpur. m. (-रः) The same as अब्धिकफ q. v.
(according to the Rājanigh.); comp. अब्धिडिण्डिर. E.
अब्धि and हिण्डीर.

अब्ध्यग्नि Tatpur. m. (-ग्निः) Submarine fire; comp. समुद्रवह्नि.
E. अब्धि and अग्नि.
